observations: Files I opened and looked at with Read: output/page-01.png to page-08.png (all eight final pages, each viewed in full); assets/panels/03-2.png; assets/panels/03-5.png; assets/characters/checkin-patients.png; source/original.txt; source/REVISION-2026-11-11.md; and the request JSON, including the script dialogue and the recorded first reading. I did not open the other panel PNGs, the workflow/review PNGs, the storyboard SVGs, reader.html or manga.pdf. I make no claim about them.

The first reader's Priya hairstyle concern is a real visible defect, but it comes from the lettering, not the art. In the accepted art assets/panels/03-2.png, Priya has a high ponytail with a blue scrunchie at the crown, which matches checkin-patients.png and her look in 03-5.png (high ponytail, blue scrunchie). On the final page-03.png, the 03-2 caption box 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' (about y40-145) covers the top of her head, the scrunchie and the ponytail's base. Only the loose wavy lengths framing her face and shoulder show, so on the page she reads as wearing her hair down. In 03-3 (a small background figure) and 03-5 the ponytail and clip are visible. So on the page her hair appears to change twice within page 3.

Every line of text on all eight pages matches the script, and every script line matches the source text word for word: captions, balloons, labels and the TV/tablet labels 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12', 'NOW · A-12' and 'RAVI · READY'. The page 5 and 6 labels use the full wording the user approved ('add page if needed'), with the corrections recorded in source review r7 (odontogram, growth scales, Paediatrician). The added consent exchange in 05-2 follows the user's 2026-11-12 follow-up.

Tails and speakers, checked page by page: 01-2 both tails go to Meera; 01-3 to Ananya; 02-2 to Ananya; 02-3 to Meera; 02-4 to Ananya (seated left), and the balloon sits between the two figures but the tail is clear; 04-2 to the nurse; 05-1 to Ananya; 05-2 'May the AI...' to Ananya and 'Yes, I agree.' by a long diagonal tail to Ravi on the right; 05-3 to Ravi; 06-2 to Ananya; 07-1 and 07-3 to Meera; 07-2 to Ravi. No balloon or caption covers a face.

Character continuity, checked by eye: Ananya keeps the low bun, gold stud, teal kurta, white coat and an unused stethoscope on pages 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. In 02-4 her face reads slightly rounder and her bun looser than in 02-1/02-2, but the costume, stud and stethoscope match, so she is still identifiable. Meera keeps her left-shoulder braid and blue print kurta, with the bangle visible in 01-2, 07-1, 07-3 and 08-4. Ravi keeps his sage shirt, left-wrist watch and brown shoulder bag (shoulder, then lap in 03-5, floor in 04-2, beside the chair on pages 5 and 6). Mr. Raman keeps his glasses, cream shirt and cane in 03-1, 03-3 and 03-5. The nurse matches her cast description (lavender scrubs, bob, lanyard, watch). In 08-2 and 08-3 the soft rounded vignette and the lighter palette set the vision panels apart from the present-day panels.
Pages 1, 2 and 4-8 read cleanly in their intended left-to-right, top-to-bottom order. The only open problem is the 03-2 occlusion, which creates a visible continuity break for the reader.

issues.problem: On the final page, the 03-2 caption box covers Priya's blue scrunchie and the base of her high ponytail. She therefore appears to wear her hair loose in 03-2, but has a high ponytail with a blue clip in 03-3 (background) and 03-5. The accepted art is consistent, but the lettered page shows a hairstyle mismatch within the same page, which the first reader reported. Fix: move or reshape the 03-2 caption, for example a shorter or wider box placed higher in the open sky at upper left, or adjust the panel crop, so that the scrunchie and ponytail crown stay visible. Then re-render page 3, the PDF and the reader, and re-review.

Close-up of the same laptop with the doctor's hand on the trackpad. This is the screen walkthrough the user asked for in Request 3 and the 'add page if needed' follow-up. It is a product aside rather than Ravi-specific care, as the source intends.

The cut to the reception counter (same chairs, monitor and waiting patients as page 3) reads as checkout after the consult. The source has no transition caption here, and the setting makes the move clear.

The WELBUK VISION label, the pale vignette and the lighter palette mark it as a vision. The specialist and connected clinics fit the caption.

Returns to the clinic exterior for the closing group portrait. The '•' separators are the source's own wording for this label. The panel works as a symbolic ending, not a timed scene.

readingReview.comparison: Agreements with the first reading: the reading order on all pages, the speaker attribution, and the absence of covered faces. Judgement on each concern the first reader raised: (p1) Meera is unnamed: acceptable, because the source gives no dialogue that names her. (p2) No evening caption: acceptable, because the source caption is kept word for word and the sunset window is clear. The CARE label over Meera's lower kurta: acceptable, because her protected phone hand is clear. The top caption touching Ananya's hair: minor, with no feature hidden. Ananya's face in 02-4: a mild drift, acceptable because her costume, bun and stud identify her. (p3) QR 'at the door': acceptable, because the stand is just inside the glass entrance as scripted. Ravi named by caption and A-12 inferred: both are source text, and 04-1 confirms A-12. Priya's hairstyle: confirmed as a defect. It is not in the art (03-2.png has the high ponytail and blue scrunchie) but is caused by the 03-2 caption covering them, so this is unresolved. (p4) The nurse is unintroduced: acceptable, because her scrubs show her role. The 'RAVI ·' / 'READY' break: source label word for word, and the trailing-dot line break matches the label style elsewhere, so acceptable. (p5) The delayed answer: required by the user's consent decision. The reply balloon's position: resolved by its tail and Ravi's gesture. Dense jargon: the full wording the user asked for. (p6) A specialty showcase unrelated to Ravi: explicitly requested by the user (Request 3). The label overhang: cosmetic. (p7) The scene jump and the walkthrough not drawn: source text word for word, and the setting carries the reader. (p8) 'Tomorrow/us', the repeated VISION label, the '•' separators, the family and specialist, and Ravi's outfit: all source text or deliberate vision marking. The caption over the feet: minor. One difference stays open, the 03-2 hairstyle occlusion, so the status is changes-requested.
